report.headline: Usage projected to drop from 23.9% to 18.7%, below the NBA average, while the shooting projection is not trustworthy

projection.text: Player A's usage rate is projected to fall from 23.9% in the EuroLeague to 18.7% in the NBA, below the league average of 20.0% and well under the z-preservation baseline of 24.5% that would hold if his standing above the EuroLeague average carried over unchanged.

risks.text: Projected usage of 18.7% is below the NBA average of 20.0%, and the 80% interval (13.4%-24.0%) spans nearly the entire one-standard-deviation band of the league (5.3%), so the model cannot distinguish a below-average from a roughly average usage outcome for him.
The true shooting model has a 4.7% mean absolute error, identical to simply predicting the league mean, so the projected 54.7% true shooting figure carries no real information.
The estimate rests on only 61 historical EL->NBA transitions, a modest sample underlying fitted carry-over slopes of 0.58 for usage and 0.754 for true shooting.
Even the usage-rate model, which does beat its baseline, still carries a 3.3% mean absolute error against a league standard deviation of only 5.3%.

strengths.text: In the EuroLeague he posted a 31.4% assist rate and 6.0 assists per 75 possessions, indicating a significant play-making role.
His true shooting percentage of 61.2% was 0.66 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average, reflecting efficient scoring in that role.

His usage rate of 23.9% sat 0.84 standard deviations above the EuroLeague average, well above even the +0.46 sd typical of players who make this move, marking him as a heavy-usage player even within a selected group.
He maintained a moderate 16.3% turnover rate despite carrying a high share of the offense.

uncertainty.text: The 80% interval for usage rate runs from 13.4% to 24.0%, a band nearly as wide as the league's full standard deviation of 5.3%, so the model can rank him but not price him precisely; separately, the true shooting projection of 54.7% should not be relied on because its error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league mean (4.7%).
